key_insight: Oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group metal oxides are largely captured by two bulk descriptors: crystal reduction potential and band gap.
engineering_relevance: Bulk-property estimates could accelerate oxide screening for energy technologies, although the study does not directly evaluate solar-cell performance.
method: Survey 39 oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Use ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed neutral oxygen-vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model and retain its two dominant descriptors.
evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: Predictions require caution when vacancy electrons are accommodated through mechanisms other than cation reduction.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
